_purpose: Transport ensemble member for the sampling-plan spread analysis.
Hydrodynamic solution: 40_highres_novfilt from the model-configuration comparison,
seasonal temperature RMSE 1.3619 degC against the profiler record,
within a factor of two of the best seasonal RMSE.
Every member releases the same 1.0 g/s of nitrogen into the same cell from
04:00 to 05:00 on 1 August 2024 and differs only in the flow solution that
carries it, so the spread among them measures sensitivity of the predicted
Run with, in the model-running repository (<RUNNER>), which is not published:
_note_initialLayerDepths: Forty z-layers. Every initial condition is zero, so this list only has to
exist and be monotonic; it carries no information about the vertical grid.
_note_balanceOutput: Off, to match the archived run this validates against.
_note_obsPoints: The five monitoring cells of the run this validates against: segments 399,
430, 4658, 4436 and 718, given here as the lon/lat of each cell centre. The
archived run names them ObsPoint 1-5; the names used here are the ones the
committed series carry, assigned by matching values, not by position.
_note_scheme: 15.7, not 15. The integer part selects the iterative GMRES solver; the
digits after the point are flags the kernel reads as bits 0-2 of intopt:
no dispersion at zero flow, no dispersion across open boundaries, and a
lower-order scheme at open boundaries. All three are set in the run this
validates against, and they change the transport matrix, so a bare 15
_note_load: One-hour pulse of 1.0 g/s into cTR1, dTR1 and dTR3, block interpolation.
cTR1 carries no reaction; dTR1 and dTR3 decay at the two rates set in the
dynamics file. cTR2, cTR3 and dTR2 are unused: the process library defines
no decay-rate constant for tracer 2, and one conservative tracer is enough.
No FLOW column, so the values are mass loads and Block 6 carries no CONC.
_note_mapTimeStep: Daily. The spread score is evaluated on the final full-domain field only,
so hourly maps would cost gigabytes of output that nothing reads.
_note_timeStep1: The coupling supplies volumes, areas and flows once a day and DELWAQ
interpolates between those breakpoints. The calculation step is an hour so
that the one-hour release is resolved rather than smeared across a whole
coupling interval; 3600 divides 86400 exactly, as DELWAQ requires.
_note_outputSteps: Output matches the daily coupling interval. A coupling that supplies flows
once a day carries no information between its breakpoints for finer output
to report, and the preflight requires whole multiples of that interval.
